name: David Capstick
title: Clinical Psychologist, Psychologist
description: Dave strongly focuses his practice within the LGBTQIAP+ community. He has a clinical and research background in how gender and sexuality influence mental health. Dave works across most psychological disorders but has a particular interest in issues related to trauma, attachment, self-worth/self-esteem, substance-related issues (particularly crystal methamphetamine), and relationship problems. Dave is an advanced level Certified Schema Therapist, and his main approaches are schema therapy, Emotion Focused Therapy (EFT), Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), EMDR, and Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT).
specialties: Trauma, attachment, self-worth/self-esteem, substance-related issues (particularly crystal methamphetamine), and relationship problems.

name: Owen O'Neil
title: Psychologist
description: He is a proud queer poly person who is dedicated to working with members of queer communities to empower them to improve their wellbeing and thrive. He provides individual therapy and relationship therapy, particularly with queer, poly, and CNM relationships. He has a special interest in complex trauma and addiction issues. Owen is a trauma-informed, gender-affirming, sex, kink, and sex worker positive, and neurodiversity affirming practitioner.
specialties: Complex trauma, LGBTIQAP+, brothaboy and sistagirl communities, Drug and alcohol issues, Relationship counselling, including with queer couples and people in poly relationships

name: Lilly McCann
title: Psychologist
description: Lilly is a warm and dedicated psychologist who is passionate about supporting children, adolescents, and adults to create a safe, collaborative, and trauma-informed space where clients feel supported to explore their challenges and make meaningful change. As a queer ADHDer, Lilly brings lived experience to her practice and is committed to providing inclusive and affirming support to LGBTQIAP+ clients.
specialties: Mood and anxiety disorders, interpersonal difficulties, stress, relationship and attachment concerns, school avoidance, and PDA (Persistent Drive for Autonomy).

name: Cait Barr
title: Psychologist
description: In particular, Cait enjoys supporting clients in longer term work, helping with anxiety, depression, grief and loss, stress, life adjustments, interpersonal struggles, trauma, ones relationship with oneself, identity and self-esteem, LGBTQIA+ issues, and disordered eating including ones relationship with food and body. Cait has a special interest in working with queer women.
specialties: Anxiety, depression, grief and loss, stress, life adjustments, interpersonal struggles, trauma, ones relationship with oneself, identity and self-esteem, LGBTQIA+ issues, and disordered eating including ones relationship with food and body. Cait has a special interest in working with queer women.

name: Holly Pretorius
title: Psychologist
description: Holly particularly enjoys working with neurodivergent and LGBTQIAP+ adolescents. Holly herself is proudly queer and autistic; this lived experience adds to her authentic, empathetic, and client-centred approach. Holly’s practice incorporates evidence-based therapeutic modalities including Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT), Schema Therapy, and Humanistic Therapy.
specialties: Anxiety, depression, interpersonal challenges, identity exploration, school can’t, and self-esteem issues. Holly particularly enjoys working with neurodivergent and LGBTQIAP+ adolescents.

name: Jhocelyn Jobe
title: Psychologist
description: She endeavours to help her clients feel seen and heard in their experiences, and enjoys working with her fellow LGBTQIAP+ community members from a standpoint that is neurodiverse affirming and trauma informed.‍ Jhocelyn has particular interest in supporting individuals who have come into their neurodivergent diagnosis during their adult life, working with her clients to build on their strengths and self-advocacy. She’s also passionate in applying her Emotion Focused Therapy (EFT) skills to relationship counselling, inclusive of diverse relationship structures and kink dynamics.‍ Jhocelyn welcomes both adolescents (16+) and adults to her therapy space. In addition she has experience supporting individuals with: anxiety, stress, phobias, interpersonal issues, LGBTQIAP+ exploration, trauma, attachment issues and self-esteem concerns. She is also available to conduct Adult WPATH assessments
specialties: Anxiety, stress, phobias, interpersonal issues, LGBTQIAP+ exploration, trauma, attachment issues and self-esteem concerns.

name: David Edmonds
title: Psychologist
description: David provides a warm, caring, and non-judgemental therapeutic approach to therapy that draws from various evidence-based treatments including Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT), Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Dialectical Behaviour Therapy (DBT), Eye Movement Desensitisation and Reprocessing (EMDR), and Motivational Interviewing. ‍David has experience working with children, adolescents and adults, through a range of presentations including depression, anxiety, stress, self-esteem, trauma, personality disorders, neurodiversity, aging, relationship difficulties, body image, sleep, and anger. David enjoys working collaboratively with clients to improve their wellbeing and has a special interest in working with individuals who also belong to the LGBTIQAP+ community and/or neurodivergent individuals who may face unique challenges.
specialties: Depression, anxiety, stress, self-esteem, trauma, personality disorders, neurodiversity, aging, relationship difficulties, body image, sleep, and anger.

name: Sophie Glynn
title: Psychologist
description: Sophie has a particular interest in working with LGBTQIAP+ people and has experience supporting adolescent and adult clients with a range of concerns.
specialties: Working with LGBTQIAP+ people and has experience supporting adolescent and adult clients with a range of concerns.

name: Bill Darby
title: Psychologist
description: He works with people of all backgrounds, and is sensitive to the experiences of LGBTIQAP+ people, people from diverse and minority backgrounds, and those experiencing challenges around anxiety, trauma, gender, sexuality, and relationships (including non-traditional relationships).
specialties: Anxiety, trauma, gender, sexuality, and relationships (including non-traditional relationships).

name: Serena Hillin
title: Psychologist
description: As a non-binary and neurodivergent individual, they welcome clients who are experiencing difficulties with their identity, mental health, or life path. ‍Serena draws upon Cognitive-Behavioural Therapy (CBT), Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Interpersonal Therapy (IPT), LGBTQIA+ Affirmative Therapy, Internal Family Systems Therapy (Parts Work), and Narrative Therapy to help clients in a way that identifies their unique strengths and empowers them to feel more confident in resolving their challenges.
specialties: They welcome clients who are experiencing difficulties with their identity, mental health, or life path, working with individuals from ages 8 - 80. Using Cognitive-Behavioural Therapy (CBT), Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Interpersonal Therapy (IPT), LGBTQIA+ Affirmative Therapy, Internal Family Systems Therapy (Parts Work), and Narrative Therapy

name: Emily Alexander
title: Psychologist
description: ‍Emily is especially passionate about helping neurodivergent LGBTQIAP+ folk work towards self-acceptance and authenticity.
specialties: Neurodiversity. She provides psychological assessments to children (aged 10+), adolescents, and adults, including autism, ADHD, dyslexia, cognitive, and academic assessments.

name: Logan Flott
title: Psychologist
description: Now based in Australia, Logan has achieved full registration as a psychologist, where she continues to pursue her passion for inclusive, trauma-informed care. She is particularly passionate about providing therapeutic support from an intersectional perspective to neurodivergent individuals and those within the LGBT+ community, offering a safe, affirming space where clients can explore their unique experiences and challenges. While Logan’s experience spans a wide range of presentations, she has developed a particular love in supporting individuals navigating experiences of complex trauma, eating disorders (particularly ARFID and restrictive eating disorders), self-harm, and psychosis.
specialties: Complex trauma, eating disorders (particularly ARFID and restrictive eating disorders), self-harm, and psychosis.

name: Dilay Tuncel
title: Psychologist
description: Dee is LGBTQIAP+ inclusive, sex-positive, and kink-positive, and welcomes clients aged 15+ from all walks of life.
specialties: Anxiety, depression, relationship/attachment issues, stress, grief, anger, neurodiversity, and major life transitions (hello, quarter-life crisis or career pivot!).

name: Rene Pirrotta
title: Psychologist
description: She works with various psychological concerns in adults, including trauma, substance-related concerns, attachment, difficulties with emotional regulation and self-esteem. Rene has experience working with clients exploring their gender, sexuality, and neurodivergent identity. Rene approaches therapy in a collaborative manner, drawing upon a range of evidence-based treatment models, with a focus on Schema Therapy, EMDR and Dialectical Behaviour Therapy (DBT).
specialties: Trauma, substance-related concerns, attachment, difficulties with emotional regulation and self-esteem.

name: Steph Sier
title: Social Worker
description: Steph is an LGBTQIAP+ affirmative therapist. She works across various psychological difficulties (including depression, anxiety, PTSD/trauma, personality disorders, self-esteem issues, and many others) and uses various psychological therapies (including ACT, CBT, DBT, and mindfulness) and a qualified EMDR therapist.
specialties: Depression, anxiety, PTSD/trauma, personality disorders, self-esteem issues, and many others) and uses various psychological therapies (including ACT, CBT, DBT, and mindfulness) and a qualified EMDR therapist.

name: Stanley Chin
title: Psychologist
description: Stanley is a non-binary/transfeminine psychologist who aims to hold a safe space to provide a warm and non-judgmental approach to walk alongside clients aged 14 and above. ‍Stanley has experience supporting people with many challenges including gender, sexuality, loss/grief, anxiety, low mood, relationships, stress, and self-care. Stanley also has experience providing WPATH-guided informed consent discussions with adolescents and adults and supports them to access gender-affirming healthcare.
specialties: Gender, sexuality, loss/grief, anxiety, low mood, relationships, stress, and self-care.

name: Kate Langtry
title: Psychologist
description: Her therapeutic work draws on Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT), Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Dialectical Behaviour Therapy (DBT), and trauma-informed approaches, allowing therapy to be tailored to each person’s unique needs.
specialties: Anxiety and stress, depression and low mood, emotional regulation, self-esteem and identity, body image, and life transitions.

name: Halo Jones
title: Psychologist
description: Halo’s work is informed by a lifetime of lived experience as a queer and transgender woman. Halo believes strongly in the human and social rights of gender and sexual minority groups, and recognizes the need for representation within healthcare. Halo recognizes the different and changing needs of people within the LGBTIQAP+ community.
specialties: Working with TGD and neurodiverse people in order to help them face their challenges, celebrate their milestones, and discover, explore, and live their authentic and unique lives.

name: Ritchie Wong
title: Psychologist
description: Ritchie is a Psychologist and EMDR Practitioner in Melbourne who has been working with people of all ages from diverse cultural backgrounds who present with various issues at different stages of their lives. Ritchie incorporates various evidence-based treatments including EMDR therapy, Cognitive Behavioural Therapy, Mindfulness, Relaxation, Hypnosis and Ego State Therapy to ensure that clients obtain a carefully-tailored experience with the best possible outcomes. He is experienced at dealing with a range of mental health issues but has a particular interest in the treatment of PTSD, childhood trauma, abuse and long-standing chronic depression and anxiety.
specialties: PTSD, Complex Trauma, earlier-life (childhood) trauma and abuse.

name: Shelley Amity
title: Psychologist
description: Hello I'm a mindful registered psychologist with a wealth of clinical experience and has specialised in EMDR Therapy for Trauma, PTSD, Anxiety, Depression, Grief & Loss and more. Aiming to help adults from all walks of life to overcome psychological distress and trauma, develop essential coping skills and step-by-step strategies, to achieve a meaningful, happier, and healthier live.
specialties:
“Be yourself, everything else is taken”, Oscar Wild.
I encourage each client to identify their uniqueness and being unafraid to express their individuality to create an independent and meaningful life.
Overall, I have extensive clinical experience working with a diverse client group with complex presentation, such as victims of trauma in the context of my previous role at the Trauma Centre of Aust

name: Kaveh Kawa Bevrani
title: Counsellor, Social Worker
description: Kawa / Kaveh is a compassionate mental health clinician with over seven years’ experience supporting individuals through anxiety, depression, trauma, and life challenges. Kawa works with people experiencing a wide range of difficulties, including emotional overwhelm, relationship struggles, low self-esteem, the effects of past trauma, and ongoing stress. He has particular expertise in working with complex and developmental trauma, including experiences of childhood abuse or neglect, as well as sexual assault, domestic violence, and alcohol and other drug (AOD) concerns. His work is grounded in attachment-informed, client-centred, and evidence-based approaches, drawing on therapies such as EMDR, Schema Therapy, ACT, DBT, MBT, Ego-State Therapy, and CBT.
specialties: Trauma-focused therapy, attachment-informed practice, personality disorders, parenting, and a diverse range of therapy modalities including psychodynamic, CBT, DBT, IFS, IPT, ACT, schema therapy, and polyvagal theory.

name: Kay-Sheree Spurling
title: Psychologist
description: My areas of interest are adult ADHD, ASD, substance misuse, trauma, challenging behaviour and all things anxiety. My practice is trauma informed, neuro affirming and I welcome LGBTIQ client's.
specialties: Anxiety, ADHD, ASD, Addiction, Trauma, Depression, behavioural concerns, adjustment to parenthood, workplace issues, burnout, and managing life transitions. I use interpersonal therapy, schema therapy, client focused therapy, CBT, ACT and DBT to support adolescent and adult clients.
